rows.description: I ask the AI before I even try, and my own thinking feels slower. Wise: try first, use AI to check or explore, and keep skills I want to own. Harmful: submitting what I do not understand.

rows.description: The AI answers confidently and I accept it. Wise: trust but verify, especially for facts, health, law and money; ask for sources and test claims. Harmful: treating fluent text as truth.

rows.description: Talking to an AI companion feels easier than people, since it never judges me. Wise: enjoy the comfort but keep human bonds growing, as real friends can hold me in ways software cannot. Harmful: replacing all relationships with it.

rows.description: My professor suspects that my assignment was AI-written when partly it was. I feel exposed. Wise: be honest, show my process, and learn the rules. Harmful: lying, which turns a minor matter into a serious one.

rows.description: A classmate finishes work in minutes with AI and scores well, and I feel foolish for working hard. Wise: shortcuts show in interviews and later work; build real skill, use AI as a tutor. Harmful: copying blindly to keep up.

rows.description: I worry AI will take the job I am training for. The anxiety is understandable. Wise: learn the tools, build judgement and human skills, and stay adaptable. Harmful: freezing or denying the change.

rows.description: My employer expects me to produce AI-level output at speed and never asks whether I understand. Wise: check accuracy myself and speak up about errors. Harmful: hiding behind the tool when mistakes occur.

rows.description: What began as an occasional drink, vape or game night has become how I cope, and I keep saying I can stop anytime. Wise: honestly count the cost, tell someone safe, seek professional help early. Harmful: hiding it and calling it stress relief.
